sentences.text:
Indian Penal Code vs In Re : Jayanta Kumar Mridha on 19 May,
2023
Author: Debangsu Basak

Bench: Debangsu Basak 19.05.2023 KAUSHIK Allowed C.R.M.(A) 2104 of 2023 In Re:- An application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with Palashipara Police Station Case No. 72 of 2023 dated 01.03.2023 under Sections 420/465/467/468/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

And In Re : Jayanta Kumar Mridha ...... petitioner Mr. Arindam Jana Mr. S. S. Mondal Mr. A. Das Sharma Mr. P. P. Sinha ....for the petitioner Mr. Sudip Majumder ....for the defacto complainant in person Mr. Neguive Ahmed Ms. Amita Gour ....for the State Petitioner and the State are represented.
There are disputes between the private parties with regard to an immovable property.
Apparently, allegations relate to recording of name in the records of the Block Land and Land Reforms Office.
Record of rights, per se, does not confer title on the person whose name is recorded.
The civil disputes are yet to be adjudicated upon by the competent Court.
Criminal liability, if there be any, will follow the civil liability, if there be any.
In such circumstances, we grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest the petitioner shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each, to the satisfaction of the arresting officer and also be subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and on further condition that the petitioner shall meet the Investigating Officer as and when called for till the conclusion of the investigation and on condition that the petitioner shall appear on every date before the jurisdictional Court on and from the date fixed for appearance of the accused and in default the jurisdictional Court will pass appropriate order to secure the presence of the petitioner in Court including cancelling the anticipatory bail granted without further reference to this Court.
This application for anticipatory bail is, thus, allowed.
(Debangsu Basak, J.) (Md. Shabbar Rashidi, J.)
